findings.title: Adding an abstract method breaks existing CryptoProvider implementations
findings.body: `order()` is a new abstract SPI method, so any provider implementation compiled against the previous interface must add this method before it can compile against this version. This is a source- and binary-compatibility break for third-party crypto providers; make it a default method (or otherwise preserve compatibility) if existing providers are expected to keep working.

findings.title: Sequence parsing does not enforce the declared sequence boundary
findings.body: The loop subtracts each child's full encoded length but never checks whether that length exceeds the remaining sequence length. A child that extends past the declared sequence boundary is therefore accepted, and parsing continues over bytes outside the sequence. Since this decoder handles ECDSA signature encodings, malformed input can be interpreted as a valid pair of integers instead of being rejected. Reject a child whose encoded length exceeds the remaining sequence bytes and verify the sequence is fully consumed.
